parts.zh: M: 欢迎收听《读书俱乐部》
W: 我认为这是因为我传达的理念
M: 你自己也曾陷入过那种循环
W: 的确如此。我赚了几百万美元
M: 那么，你是如何摆脱这种模式的？你又会建议其他人怎么做？
W: 首先要改变的是我们的价值观
M: 这要如何落实到实际行动上？你能不能举些例子
W: 通常需要采取行动的主要方面是住房
M: 听起来这都是很大的牺牲

items.stem: What message does the woman convey in her book?

choices.text: Prioritizing happiness over money.
choices.zh: 把幸福置于金钱之上。

choices.text: Joining the club to get her new book.
choices.zh: 加入俱乐部以获得她的新书。

choices.text: Managing one's personal finances wisely.
choices.zh: 明智地管理个人财务。

choices.text: Consuming more only when earning more.
choices.zh: 只有在挣得更多时才消费更多。

items.stem: What do we learn about the woman before she became a writer?

choices.text: She was in debt.
choices.zh: 她负债累累。

choices.text: She was a financial adviser.
choices.zh: 她是一名理财顾问。

choices.text: She earned $30,000 a month.
choices.zh: 她每月挣3万美元。

choices.text: She enjoyed a happy life.
choices.zh: 她享有幸福的生活。

items.stem: What does the woman say about one's financial behavior?

choices.text: It reflects one's earning power.
choices.zh: 它反映一个人的挣钱能力。

choices.text: It varies with one's environment.
choices.zh: 它随一个人所处的环境而变化。

choices.text: It mirrors one's sense of well-being.
choices.zh: 它反映一个人的幸福感。

choices.text: It changes with one's goals in life.
choices.zh: 它随一个人的人生目标而改变。

items.stem: What does the man say about sharing a home?

choices.text: It would give him more time to be with his loved ones.
choices.zh: 这会让他有更多时间陪伴所爱的人。

choices.text: It would be good for those who value relationships.
choices.zh: 这对重视人际关系的人有好处。

choices.text: It would mean major sacrifices for him.
choices.zh: 这对他来说意味着重大牺牲。

choices.text: It would deprive him of his individuality.
choices.zh: 这会剥夺他的个性。

items.stem: What do we learn about one of the newest additions to the gallery's collection?

choices.text: It was the artist's first landscape.
choices.zh: 这是该艺术家的第一幅风景画。

choices.text: It was a painting by Christopher.
choices.zh: 这是Christopher的一幅画作。

choices.text: It was donated by the artist herself.
choices.zh: 这是由艺术家本人捐赠的。

choices.text: It was displayed at a retirement party.
choices.zh: 这在一次退休派对上展出过。

items.stem: What does the man say about one of the most acclaimed paintings by Danielle Gregory?

choices.text: It was the painting that instantly made her rich.
choices.zh: 正是这幅画让她立刻变得富有。

choices.text: It has cost him a lot of money to purchase it.
choices.zh: 他花了很多钱来购买它。

choices.text: It was recently purchased by the gallery.
choices.zh: 这是画廊最近购入的。

choices.text: It is owned by an anonymous collector.
choices.zh: 它为一位匿名收藏家所有。

items.stem: Why does the woman say she can feel immersed in the scene in the painting?

choices.text: It reflects her emotions.
choices.zh: 它反映了她的情感。

choices.text: It contains ample details.
choices.zh: 它包含大量细节。

choices.text: It appears perfectly symmetrical.
choices.zh: 它看起来完全对称。

choices.text: It depicts the beauty of desolation.
choices.zh: 它描绘了荒凉之美。

items.stem: How does the man describe Danielle Gregory?

choices.text: She is eccentric like any other artist.
choices.zh: 她像任何其他艺术家一样古怪。

choices.text: She is a very nice and intelligent artist.
choices.zh: 她是一位非常好且聪明的艺术家。

choices.text: She is as lucky as any acclaimed artist.
choices.zh: 她像任何受赞誉的艺术家一样幸运。

choices.text: She is one of the most productive artists.
choices.zh: 她是最多产的艺术家之一。

items.stem: What does the passage say about forgiveness?

choices.text: It is vital to one's mental health.
choices.zh: 它对一个人的心理健康至关重要。

choices.text: It leads to reconciliation and peace.
choices.zh: 它带来和解与和平。

choices.text: It promotes interpersonal relationship.
choices.zh: 它促进人际关系。

choices.text: It keeps one from traumatic experience.
choices.zh: 它使人免受创伤经历的困扰。

items.stem: When is forgiveness especially challenging?

choices.text: When the offender has power over the victim.
choices.zh: 当冒犯者对受害者拥有权力时。

choices.text: When the offender is not willing to apologize.
choices.zh: 当冒犯者不愿意道歉时。

choices.text: When the offender is not duly penalized.
choices.zh: 当冒犯者未受到应有的惩罚时。

choices.text: When the offender adds insult to injury.
choices.zh: 当冒犯者雪上加霜时。

items.stem: What should one do in order to forgive the offender?

choices.text: Talk with the offender calmly.
choices.zh: 平静地与冒犯者交谈。

choices.text: Accept the offender's apology.
choices.zh: 接受冒犯者的道歉。

choices.text: Find out why he committed the offense.
choices.zh: 找出他为什么犯下过错。

choices.text: Determine how serious the offense was.
choices.zh: 确定过错有多严重。

items.stem: What does the passage say about the Glasgow subway in the 1960s?

choices.text: The number of passengers dropped sharply.
choices.zh: 乘客数量急剧下降。

choices.text: It served more and more commuters.
choices.zh: 它服务的通勤者越来越多。

choices.text: The number of stations increased to 50.
choices.zh: 车站数量增加到50个。

choices.text: It became the longest in the United Kingdom.
choices.zh: 它成为英国最长的地铁。

items.stem: Why was the Glasgow subway closed in 1977?

choices.text: To increase capacity to meet growing needs.
choices.zh: 为了增加运力以满足日益增长的需求。

choices.text: To make way for other means of transport.
choices.zh: 为了给其他交通方式让路。

choices.text: To have its systems modernised.
choices.zh: 为了使其系统现代化。

choices.text: To avoid further financial losses.
choices.zh: 为了避免进一步的财务损失。

items.stem: Why does the Glasgow subway remain important today?

choices.text: It is generally recognised as a world heritage site.
choices.zh: 它被普遍认可为世界遗产。

choices.text: It is the fastest way to reach the city's south side.
choices.zh: 它是到达城市南部的最快方式。

choices.text: It constitutes a source of revenue for the city.
choices.zh: 它构成该城市的一项收入来源。

choices.text: It helps reduce traffic jams in the city centre.
choices.zh: 它有助于减少市中心的交通拥堵。

items.stem: What does the passage say about all subway stations in Glasgow nowadays?

choices.text: They are usually crowded.
choices.zh: 它们通常很拥挤。

choices.text: They use high-tech systems.
choices.zh: 它们使用高科技系统。

choices.text: They accept smartcards only.
choices.zh: 它们只接受智能卡。

choices.text: They are colourfully decorated.
choices.zh: 它们装饰得色彩鲜艳。

items.stem: What does the speaker say about the bears in national parks now?

choices.text: They are quite friendly to humans.
choices.zh: 它们对人类相当友好。

choices.text: They are shrinking in numbers.
choices.zh: 它们的数量正在减少。

choices.text: They are unafraid of humans.
choices.zh: 它们不怕人类。

choices.text: They are especially fond of garbage.
choices.zh: 它们特别喜欢垃圾。

items.stem: What does the speaker say about visitors feeding bears in national parks?

choices.text: It is strictly forbidden.
choices.zh: 这是严格禁止的。

choices.text: It is an uncommon sight.
choices.zh: 这是不常见的景象。

choices.text: It is a gesture of human generosity.
choices.zh: 这是人类慷慨的表现。

choices.text: It is allowed only in certain areas.
choices.zh: 只允许在特定区域这样做。

items.stem: What is the speaker's advice to people who carry some food while hiking on a park trail?

choices.text: Share their food with the bear they see.
choices.zh: 与看到的熊分享食物。

choices.text: Be prepared to run into a hungry bear.
choices.zh: 做好遇到饥饿的熊的准备。

choices.text: Try to be friendly with the bear they meet.
choices.zh: 尽量与遇到的熊友好相处。

choices.text: Refrain from teasing bears with cubs.
choices.zh: 避免逗弄带幼崽的熊。

items.stem: What does the speaker say about prejudice?

choices.text: It refers to opinions that are radical and widespread.
choices.zh: 它指的是激进且广泛存在的观点。

choices.text: It means making judgments without adequate knowledge.
choices.zh: 它意味着在没有充分了解的情况下做出判断。

choices.text: It refers to deep-rooted beliefs about someone or something.
choices.zh: 它指的是关于某人或某事的根深蒂固的信念。

choices.text: It means sticking to one's judgments even when proved wrong.
choices.zh: 它意味着即使被证明是错误的也坚持自己的判断。

items.stem: Why does the speaker say prejudiced attitudes are dangerous?

choices.text: They often lead to war between religious groups.
choices.zh: 它们常常导致宗教团体之间的战争。

choices.text: They keep certain occupations from thriving.
choices.zh: 它们阻碍某些职业的繁荣发展。

choices.text: They allow myths and half-truths to persist.
choices.zh: 它们使神话和半真半假的说法长期存在。

choices.text: They prevent us from getting to the truth.
choices.zh: 它们阻止我们了解真相。

items.stem: When does the speaker say we begin to develop prejudiced attitudes?

choices.text: When we start to feel superior.
choices.zh: 当我们开始感到优越时。

choices.text: When we mix with prejudiced people.
choices.zh: 当我们与有偏见的人交往时。

choices.text: When we live in an isolated neighborhood.
choices.zh: 当我们生活在一个封闭的社区时。

choices.text: When we try to keep up with those around us.
choices.zh: 当我们试图跟上周围的人时。

items.stem: How did the speaker feel when he started high school?

choices.text: Motivated.
choices.zh: 有动力的。

choices.text: Disappointed.
choices.zh: 失望的。

choices.text: Perplexed.
choices.zh: 困惑的。

choices.text: Shocked.
choices.zh: 震惊的。

items.stem: What did the speaker once think of teenage friendships?

choices.text: They would change with the passage of time.
choices.zh: 它们会随着时间的流逝而改变。

choices.text: They would benefit young people's adult life.
choices.zh: 它们会对年轻人的成年生活有益。

choices.text: They would help kids grow.
choices.zh: 它们会帮助孩子们成长。

choices.text: They would last a lifetime.
choices.zh: 它们会持续一生。

items.stem: What do we learn about the speaker when he returned from the Vietnam War?

choices.text: He had become mature.
choices.zh: 他已经变得成熟了。

choices.text: He suffered poor health.
choices.zh: 他健康状况不佳。

choices.text: He had lots of stories to tell.
choices.zh: 他有很多故事要讲。

choices.text: He regretted leaving Vietnam.
choices.zh: 他后悔离开越南。

items.stem: What does the speaker try to do as a teacher?

choices.text: Make friends with his students.
choices.zh: 与他的学生交朋友。

choices.text: Show his students how to do their best.
choices.zh: 向他的学生展示如何尽力而为。

choices.text: Help his students get through the growing pains.
choices.zh: 帮助他的学生度过成长的烦恼。

choices.text: Share his personal experience with his students.
choices.zh: 与他的学生分享他的个人经历。
